{{nihongo|'''Higanotome Shrine'''|氷鉋斗賣神社}} is a shrine in {{ill|Nagano (city)|af|Nagano|an|Nagano|ar|ناغانو (ناغانو)|arz|ناجانو|ast|Nagano|az|Naqano|azb|ناقانو (شهر)|ba|Нагано|ban|Nagano, Nagano|be|Нагана|bg|Нагано (град)|bn|নাগানো|br|Nagano|ca|Nagano|ce|Нагано|ceb|Nagano Shi|cs|Nagano|da|Nagano|de|Nagano|el|Ναγκάνο|eo|Nagano|es|Nagano|et|Nagano|eu|Nagano|fa|ناگانو (شهر)|fi|Nagano|fo|Nagano|fr|Nagano|fy|Nagano (stêd)|ga|Nagano|gl|Nagano|he|נאגנו|hr|Nagano|hu|Nagano|hy|Նագանո|id|Nagano|ie|Nagano|io|Nagano|it|Nagano|ja|長野市|ka|ნაგანო (ქალაქი)|kk|Нагано|ko|나가노시|ky|Нагано|lt|Naganas|lv|Nagano|mdf|Нагана (ошсь)|mn|Нагано|mr|नागानो|mzn|ناگانو (شهر)|nl|Nagano (stad)|nn|Nagano|no|Nagano|os|Нагано|pcd|Nagano|pl|Nagano|pt|Nagano (cidade)|qu|Nagano|ro|Nagano|ru|Нагано|sc|Nagano|sco|Nagano, Nagano|sh|Nagano|simple|Nagano (city)|sk|Nagano|sl|Nagano|sr|Нагано|sv|Nagano|sw|Nagano, Nagano|szl|Nagano|tg|Нагано|th|นางาโนะ (เมือง)|tl|Lungsod ng Nagano|tr|Nagano|tt|Нагано|uk|Нагано|ur|ناگانو، ناگانو|uz|Nagano|vi|Nagano (thành phố)|war|Nagano (syudad)|wuu|长野市|zh|長野市|zh_classical|長野市|zh_min_nan|Nagano-chhī|zh_yue|長野市|qid=Q128849}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. Its {{ill|Q712534|lt=former rank}} was gōsha. {{nihongo|'''Higanotome Shrine'''|氷鉋斗賣神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].

== Overview ==
It is one of the eleven shrines of {{ill|Sarashina District, Nagano|Q7423207|qid=Q7423207}} in {{ill|Shinano Province|Q289250|qid=Q289250}} listed in the ''{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|abstract|Q11064932|fr|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|ja|延喜式神名帳|simple|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|zh|延喜式神名帳|qid=Q11064932}}''. In the {{ill|Wamyō Ruijushō|Q2702542|qid=Q2702542}}, Higano-go and Tome-go are separate, but it is thought to have been the ujigami shrine of a village where both had merged in the Heian period. There is also a theory that the place name "Higano" derives from the enshrined deity {{ill|Utsushi Hikanasaku no Mikoto|Q86736058|qid=Q86736058}}<ref>Iwao Yamato, ''A Study of Ancient Shinano History'' (Yamato Shobō, 2013)</ref>. It is also recorded in the "Suwa Shrine Shimosha Shunjū no Miya Zōgū no Shidai" of {{ill|Wii|Q8079|qid=Q8079}} (Chōkyō 2) and in a grant document to {{ill|Takeda Shingen|Q276404|qid=Q276404}} in {{ill|Gohrisch|Q6698|qid=Q6698}} (Eiroku 10). The principal deity is {{ill|Utsushi Hikanasaku no Mikoto|Q86736058|qid=Q86736058}}, ancestral deity of the Azumi no Muraji, and {{ill|Takeminakata|es|Takeminakata|hu|Takeminakata|id|Takeminakata|ja|タケミナカタ|mni|ꯇꯀꯦꯃꯤꯅꯀꯇ|pl|Takeminakata|zh|建御名方神|qid=Q9150391|lt=Takeminakata-no-Kami}} with {{ill|Yasakatome|Q9150392|qid=Q9150392}} are enshrined together in the same hall.

There is Kawanakajima Tome Shrine in Kamihigano and Higano Shrine in Nakahigano; these are presumed to be branch enshrinements made when the former single village was divided.
